newsitem.title: USA: Columbia Gas says cold weather boosted Q2.
newsitem.headline: Columbia Gas says cold weather boosted Q2.

text.p: The Columbia Gas System Inc said that the sale of natural gas from a deactivated storage field and colder than normal weather in the second quarter of 1997 boosted net income per share to 63 cents from 15 cents a year ago.
The company said net income in the second quarter rose $26.7 million from the year ago period to $34.9 million.
Columbia's transmission and storage unit's operating income rose $27 million to $66 million, including a $19.1 million gain from the sale of base gas from a Columbia Transmission storage field.

It said that colder weather, 44 percent colder than normal and 19 percent colder than the year before, lower operating and maintenance costs contributed to $21.3 million operating income for the company's distribution segment, compared with a $3.0 million loss for the year ago period, which included a $15.1 million restructuring expense.
A five percent fall in natural gas prices to $2.67 per thousand cubic feet caused a $1.0 million year-on-year decline in operating income to $5.4 million at its exploration and production unit.

Its marketing, power generation and propane business made a loss of $1.8 million, compared with a $1.2 million loss a year ago, due to lower margins for gas marketing and additional costs associated with new services.

In the first half, the gain from the sale of base natgas and the colder second quarter offset the effects of warmer-than-usual weather in the first quarter, boosting Colombia to a record six months net income of $197.6 million, or $3.57 per share, up $38.1 million, or 53 cents per share, from the previous year.

The company gained a $12.8 million tax reduction, a $5.5 million from a gain on the temporary deactivation of a storage field, the full period effect of higher rates for Columbia Transmission and Columbia Gas of Kentucky and reduced interest costs.
Restructuring costs were also lower in the first half of 1997, at $7.7 million compared with $18.6 million a year ago.
